A.explanation: About $23^{\circ}$ is half the correct value and does not follow from $0.50 \text{ m}$ divided by a $4.0 \text{ m}$ wavelength.

B.explanation: A $0.50 \text{ m}$ separation is one-eighth of the $4.0 \text{ m}$ wavelength, giving $360^{\circ}/8 = 45^{\circ}$ phase difference.

C.explanation: $90^{\circ}$ would need a quarter-wavelength separation of $1.0 \text{ m}$, not the $0.50 \text{ m}$ given.

D.explanation: $180^{\circ}$ would need a half-wavelength separation of $2.0 \text{ m}$, much larger than $0.50 \text{ m}$.

hints: Notice the wave is a radio wave in a vacuum, so its speed is $c = 3.00 \times 10^8 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ and its frequency is $75 \text{ MHz} = 75 \times 10^6 \text{ Hz}$.
Connect the $50 \text{ cm} = 0.50 \text{ m}$ separation to the wavelength using $\lambda = c/f$, then find what fraction of a wavelength $0.50 \text{ m}$ represents.
Use phase difference $= (x/\lambda) \times 360^{\circ}$ with your wavelength to convert the distance fraction into degrees.
walkthrough: Identify the data: speed $c = 3.00 \times 10^8 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, frequency $f = 75 \times 10^6 \text{ Hz}$, separation $x = 50 \text{ cm} = 0.50 \text{ m}$.
Calculate the wavelength from $\lambda = c/f$: $\lambda = (3.00 \times 10^8)/(75 \times 10^6) = 4.0 \text{ m}$.
Express the separation as a fraction of a wavelength: $x/\lambda = 0.50/4.0 = 1/8$.
Convert distance fraction to phase: one full wavelength is $360^{\circ}$, so phase difference $= (1/8) \times 360^{\circ} = 45^{\circ}$.
